text:
AcmeCorp: Hey — our app gets a mid-stream disconnect when users switch from office WiFi to mobile. We see partial JSON back (no "done" event) and the UI never resumes. Billing shows we were charged for the partial response. Can you help?

sara: Sorry about that. Can you paste a session id and the approximate timestamps? Also what client (iOS/Android/web) and SDK version?

AcmeCorp: session=acme-89f1, happened ~2024-09-15T14:22Z, iOS 17.0 in WKWebView (in-app webview), SDK 2.4. Customer reported it consistently when switching SSID -> cellular.

sara: Thanks. @mike can you triage mobile repro patterns? Do we have known WKWebView/SSO TLS socket teardown issues? :thinking:

mike: WKWebView often kills idle HTTP streams when the network stack rebinds. If the client doesn't reconnect and request resume, stream ends mid-chunk. Two quick asks: can you repro with a simple EventSource client? Also send the raw SSE payload (last few bytes) if available.

AcmeCorp: attaching last bytes: `{"choices":[{"text":"The quick brown fox jumps"}` — then socket closed. No trailing bracket.

sara: Repro steps request: 1) Start EventSource to our SSE endpoint with token header. 2) Wait until partial chunk arrives. 3) Turn off WiFi on device -> cellular. 4) Observe socket close without final event.

mike: Sharing a minimal Node repro (EventSource):
```js
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <token>' } });
es.onmessage = e => console.log("MSG", e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.log("ERR", e);
// flip network on device or simulate NAT rebind
```

ade: I ran a quick check on ingress logs for session=acme-89f1 around 2024-09-15T14:22Z — saw a TCP FIN from client and no graceful end frame from runtime. Deploy-bot: `ingress-proxy: stream-reset 502 (client-init-fin) 14:22:03Z`

ade: Likely two layers: client OS tears TCP on network rebind; intermediate proxy (corp proxy / NGiNX / ALB) has idle/keepalive timeouts and sometimes translates the close into an immediate reset. That yields a truncated SSE body.

sara: Customer asking about billing for partial outputs — is there a policy?

ade: Billing system bills per token emitted by the runtime up to the last streamed token. If the runtime never sent a trailing EOS, tokens already streamed are billable. We can consider credit for this session if it's a platform fault.

mike: Short-term workaround for mobile app: enable client-side keepalives and implement resume logic. Suggested client changes:
- Send periodic `: keepalive\n` SSE comments every 15s from client (if you control proxy) — or use a small websocket ping.
- On reconnect, call a `POST /v1/stream/resume` with last_event_id to resume generation (we have an internal resume protocol).

sara: @ade can we expose `resume` to public support customers or docs?

ade: We can enable the resume endpoint for tenants — engineering needs to toggle feature flag for background resume for hosted customers. I'll open a short ticket.

mike: Also recommend client use fetch with `keepalive: true` for fetch-based streaming clients and set socket-level SO_KEEPALIVE. On iOS WKWebView there are known edge cases; websockets are more resilient across network handoffs.

AcmeCorp: For now customer wants one-time credit if we can't guarantee resume. Happy to try workaround but need fast turn.

sara: I'll escalate billing credit for session acme-89f1 to CS+billing. @ade can you attach traces and a short triage so we can decide credit?

ade: Done — attached trace id trace-rt-4492 (internal link: https://console.redwood.internal/traces/trace-rt-4492). Notes: client FIN then immediate RST from corporate proxy. Root cause looks like client network rebind + proxy translating to RST.

mike: If engineering wants to fix at runtime: options are 1) buffer small suffix and attempt graceful shutdown with `event: error` if downstream closed, 2) support a resumable generation token so clients can reattach and continue (longer delivery). I recommend (2) as long-term.

sara: Customer asking for step-by-step to try now — what do we give them?

mike: Step-by-step workaround we can send to app devs:
1) Increase underlying socket keepalive (iOS: set TCP keepalive on NSURLSession; Android: SocketOptions).
2) If using WKWebView EventSource, migrate to WebSocket where possible.
3) Implement client reconnection: on error -> reopen connection -> POST /v1/stream/resume { session_id, last_event_id }
4) Short-term: ask users to disable ‘WiFi Assist’ for the app or avoid switching networks during long generations.

sara: I'll send that to the customer + open billing ticket. If eng-runtime wants the repro, I can provide a device with VPN to simulate corporate proxy.

ade: I'll flag eng-runtime and add logs & pcap. Tagging @mike as FYI.

mike: Thanks. If we get a reproducible pcap showing RST from proxy we can close as not platform bug, but we should still ship resume endpoint.

AcmeCorp: Thanks all — starting workaround testing now. Appreciate rapid help :pray:
